messages:
maya (eng-platform): Heads-up — saw a spike in pending GPU pods in eu-west1 this morning. Lots of nodes reporting ~1 GPU free but scheduler can't pack anything.
raj (eng-sre): Ugh that sounds like fragmentation again. Any specific node labels/taints involved?
maya (eng-platform): Lots of mixed gpu-type labels: `gpu-type: v100|a100` across the pool. Also some custom taints we added last month `dedicated=true:NoSchedule` for training tenants.
alex (eng-ml): We started requesting `resource.requests: nvidia.com/gpu: 0.5` for smaller jobs which might be causing weird packing with fractional allocation on our runtime shim. Not sure how the scheduler is interpreting that.
paula (infra): Fractional requests should be handled by our device-plugin: it rounds up to whole GPUs but the node selector rules + anti-affinity from some Deployments could be causing single-GPU holes.
maya (eng-platform): I pulled the node allocation histogram: `nodes with 0 free GPUs: 46, 1 free GPU: 73, >=2 free GPUs: 9` — we have a long tail of 1-free nodes. gpu_waste ~= 19% over 24h.
raj (eng-sre): Paste of failing pods: ```kubectl describe pod gpu-small-22
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  3s  default-scheduler  0/128 nodes are available: 73 Insufficient gpu, 55 node(s) didn't match node selector.
```
alex (eng-ml): That `node selector` mismatch is likely from some workloads pinned to `gpu-type: a100` only. Small jobs are unconstrained but scheduler prefers taint-tolerant nodes first?
paula (infra): We also have a `prefer_low_latency` affinity for a few jobs in eu-west1 to keep them inside the same AZ — that reduces packing flexibility.
maya (eng-platform): Proposal: experiment with a 'slab' allocation policy in the scheduler — group GPUs into logical slabs (1,2,4) and prefer placing small jobs into slabs rather than spreading 1 GPU across many nodes. Would reduce fragmentation.
raj (eng-sre): Slab allocator sounds promising. We should be careful about preemptions though — can we combine slabs with taint-based isolation so reserved tenants keep their slabs?
alex (eng-ml): Also would love a cheap fallback path: if exact gpu-type not available use quantized-runtime variant (lower perf) instead of leaving pods pending. Could add a toleration-based fallback in the scheduler config.
paula (infra): Short-term fix: run a descheduler job to evict low-priority burst pods that are currently occupying the only free GPU on some nodes and let higher-priority queued jobs pack.
maya (eng-platform): Agree. Short-term: descheduler + run a reclaim job. Mid-term: slab allocator + topology-aware packing. Long-term: improve quota/requests so we don't `0.5` trick.
raj (eng-sre): Action items: 1) I will schedule a descheduler run in eu-west1 tonight (11pm UTC). Owner: raj. 2) maya/paula prototype slab allocation policy in our scheduler plugin next week. 3) alex to audit ML job pod specs for `nodeSelector`/`affinity` and `requests` inconsistencies.
paula (infra): FYI cost impact estimated: fragmentation added ~+$9k/mo in idle-GPU billing for eu-west1 based on last 7 days.
maya (eng-platform): Quick config snippet we might test in the plugin: ```yaml
preferredSchedulingTerms:
- weight: 100
  preference:
    matchExpressions:
    - key: gpu-slab
      operator: In
      values: ["1","2","4"]
```
This lets the scheduler prefer slabs of size match.
alex (eng-ml): For fallback: add `nodeAffinity` with soft preference for `gpu-type: a100` and a lower weight for `a100-quant` nodes, then runtime can detect slower tensors.
raj (eng-sre): I'll monitor eviction rate, pending queue, and gpu_waste metric after the descheduler run. Please post updates here after the prototype.
maya (eng-platform): Cool. If descheduler reduces pending by >30% we consider running weekly.
paula (infra): I'll also open a ticket to standardize `requests` to integer GPUs or explicit platform-side rounding to avoid ambiguity.
maya (eng-platform): Thanks team. tagging SRE-bot to record the incident and our planned mitigations. @sre-bot please create incident note with actions.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-487 (eu-west1 GPU fragmentation). Assigned: raj. Notes attached.
